analysis:
The PR adds an optional `stopStringScope: CBv2StopStringScope?` parameter, defaulting to nil, to `EngineV2Factory.makeBridge` (EngineV2Config.swift head lines 157 and 208). It forwards the value to `EngineV2Bridge`. `EngineV2SlotFactory.makeProductionBundle` (patch near head line 574) now passes `ModelEOSPolicy.stopStringScope(modelId:modelType:)`. The rest of the visible code is unchanged. That includes the fail-loud refusal path, SSD cache close on failure, KV backend telemetry, and the prefix-cache and SSD construction relevant to T-041. The change touches no cache salt or scope derivation, no HMAC lookup naming, and no TTL, disk-budget or storage code. It adds no new network or disk surface, no keys or attestation changes, and no plaintext logging. The new parameter is a model-derived policy value, not caller-controlled, so it adds no trust-boundary input.

The change only affects the scope of stop-string matching. It could in theory change output truncation or generation termination, which affects availability or correctness (T-007, T-010) rather than confidentiality. Its effect cannot be judged from the supplied evidence because `CBv2StopStringScope`, `ModelEOSPolicy.stopStringScope`, and the `EngineV2Bridge` handling are not shown. That bridge code would need to confirm that the nil default keeps the previous behavior and that the stop-string scope cannot be influenced by consumer input to cause unbounded generation or early cutoff. No concrete regression is established in the supplied units. The base text for EngineV2SlotFactory was truncated at line 530, but the changed hunk is fully visible in the patch.
